relations.rationale: Noor's reading habits are unrelated to snacks being passed around.
Noor having read the novel twice doesn't imply anything about her asking people to quiet down.
Noor's reading habits have no bearing on house assignments of Milo and Dev.
Noor's reading habits are unrelated to Quinn's age relative to Dev.
Noor rereading the novel doesn't relate to Quinn's note-taking during the meeting.
Noor's reading habits have no connection to the number of houses in the school.
Noor reading the novel twice doesn't relate to Hana suggesting a new book.
Noor's reading habits are unrelated to Milo checking his watch.
Noor's reading habits don't connect to Milo gathering his things.
Noor's reading habits are unrelated to Dev offering to return books.
Noor's reading habits are unrelated to her thanking everyone as the meeting ends, though both involve Noor they are independent facts.
House placement of Milo and Hana is unrelated to whether the group debated the book's ending.
House assignments of Milo and Hana don't bear on Quinn's argument about the ending.
Milo and Hana being in different houses doesn't directly determine whether Hana and Dev are in different houses, since there could be three houses allowing various combinations.
House assignments are unrelated to snacks being passed around.
House assignments are unrelated to Noor asking for quiet.
Milo and Hana being in different houses doesn't determine whether Milo and Dev are in different houses.
House assignments of Milo and Hana are unrelated to Quinn's age relative to Dev.
House assignments are unrelated to Quinn's note-taking.
Milo and Hana being in different houses supports the idea that the school has multiple houses, consistent with there being three.
